json.title: Microsoft books 1.2 GW at Example Data Centers' planned AI campus in Busan
json.summary:
Microsoft has committed to 1.2 GW of capacity at an AI campus that Example Data Centers plans to build in Busan, the companies announced on Monday. Delivery starts with a 200 MW first phase targeted for ready-for-service in 2028.

Power for the site will come through a new 345 kV substation, with the grid connection secured from KEPCO. The operator plans liquid cooling for its GPU clusters and says racks drawing more than 100 kW will be supported at opening. A group of Korean lenders is putting together $2.1 billion of financing.

Example Data Centers said it picked Busan because the site sits near both the new substation and the subsea cable landing points, and that later phases will follow as more grid capacity becomes available. Scoring Wire A reports that the lease term, pricing per megawatt and the schedule beyond the first phase were not disclosed.
json.why_it_matters: Gigawatt-scale commitments from a single hyperscaler on one Korean campus are uncommon. Busan secured its grid connection outside the constrained capital region, a sign that new substations, more than land, now decide where large AI loads can go in Korea. For global operators and lenders weighing Asia-Pacific capacity, the deal sets a reference point on scale and structure.
json.expert_lens: The gap between the 1.2 GW headline and the 200 MW first phase is the figure that matters. Meeting a 2028 ready-for-service date depends on the 345 kV substation and the related grid work landing on time, a risk the announcement leaves unaddressed. Support for racks above 100 kW from opening implies a cooling design built for dense liquid-cooled GPU halls. The $2.1 billion financing looks large for a first phase alone, which suggests it may also cover later phases. The next signal is KEPCO publishing the interconnection approval for the substation.
